reviews.text:

I understand that maintaining an app costs money, and advertising can help keep the free version available. But profit should never come at the expense of Islamic values and the trust of Muslim users.

If you choose to serve the Ummah, take responsibility for the advertisements shown on your platform. Don’t force users to pay for the Pro version just to avoid content that should never have appeared in a Muslim-focused app in the first place.

This is not just a business issue; it is a matter of respect, responsibility, and trust. Please do better.

reviews.title: Disrespectful ads and an unacceptable experience!
reviews.text:
One star. I am extremely disappointed with Muslim Pro. I open this app for one simple reason: to check the prayer time. Something that should take a few seconds becomes an incredibly frustrating struggle because of intrusive advertisements. The ads feel like they go on for half an hour, and I end up having to close the app completely and reopen it just to try to see the prayer schedule. Why should anyone have to go through this to access the most basic feature of a prayer app? When you are checking how much time you have left to pray, every minute matters. These interruptions could cause someone to miss their prayer window. What makes this even more upsetting is the content of the advertisements. I have seen ads showing beer, along with other content I consider indecent and completely inappropriate for an app intended for Muslims. People open this app for prayer times, the Quran, and religious guidance. Seeing this kind of advertising in that setting is deeply disrespectful. I understand that a free app may need advertising to support its development. But that does not justify overwhelming users with ads, making essential information difficult to access, or displaying content that conflicts with the values of the audience you claim to serve.
In my experience, this app makes a simple religious routine stressful and frustrating. It feels as though advertising revenue matters more than the people relying on it. An app carrying the name “Muslim Pro” should show far greater respec

reviews.title: Inappropriate Ads on a Muslim App
reviews.text:
I appreciate many of the features this app offers, but I am deeply disappointed by the advertising experience. As a Muslim, I downloaded this app to strengthen my faith, pray, and read the Qur’an—not to be exposed to provocative advertisements.

Many of the ads, especially those from Temu, feature immodestly dressed women and content that is completely inappropriate for an Islamic app. It feels contradictory to be reading the Qur’an or preparing for salah, only to have revealing advertisements appear moments later.

I understand that the free version needs advertising to support the app, and I respect that. However, there should be a better standard for the types of ads shown. At the very least, advertisements should be family-friendly and respectful of the values of the Muslim community.

On top of that, the frequency of the ads is overwhelming. It seems like an ad appears every few seconds, making the app frustrating to use. Encouraging users to upgrade is understandable, but bombarding them with constant, inappropriate ads is not the right approach.

I hope the developers will consider implementing ad filtering for religiously appropriate content and reducing the number of ads. This would greatly improve the experience for Muslims who simply want a peaceful environment to worship and learn.

I truly hope this feedback is taken seriously, because this app has great potential.

As a woman there are times where we are not required to pray and other times we just don’t need to open the app because we see the athan notification. While it may seem trivial having an app assume you haven’t prayed or read Qur’an and tell you not to lose your progress or leave a message that begins with “⚠️” in your notifications is a bit much in my opinion. There also seems to be no way to turn these types of notifications off without turning off all of them. As much as I have loved this app in the past I think it is yet another sign for me to go analog again and carry a physical Quran and Qibla compass with me and print out prayer times for the month. May Allah bless you all for your niyah 🤲

reviews.title: Loyal User Request: Please Address Ad Overload & Khatam Bugs
reviews.text:
I have been using Muslim Pro for about 10 years, and it has always been an excellent app. The continuous updates over the years have made it even better, and I truly appreciate the effort that goes into improving it.

However, over the last two years, I’ve found myself dreading opening the app. I completely understand that advertisements generate revenue and support the platform, and I’m not asking for ads to be removed entirely. But the frequency and placement of the ads have become extremely disruptive.

For example, even when doing something simple like adjusting my phone’s brightness or navigating back to a previous page, an ad suddenly pops up. It breaks focus and makes the experience feel overwhelming. Instead of feeling seamless and spiritually uplifting, the app now feels distracting and frustrating to use. Perhaps ads could be limited to a banner at the bottom of the page or placed in a way that doesn’t interrupt core actions.

The second issue is with the Khatam feature. It appears to be glitching. It does not consistently update the Juz completed, often remaining stuck on a surah for a while. Even after closing and reopening the app, it sometimes fails to reflect the correct stopping point. This makes it difficult to trust the accuracy of the Khatam progress.

I’m sharing this feedback because I genuinely value the app and have relied on it for years. I hope these concerns can be addressed to improve the user experience.

Thank you for your time and continued effor
